4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable cartoon 2D Brotato-style plane game called “Plane Tame,” set in the Backrooms with lots of levels.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Include lots of levels and a cartoon style.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based canvas game with 10 themed rooms, auto-fire, upgrades, enemies, pickups, and a final escape.
- Assumed keyboard controls plus pointer/touch controls for mobile.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game interface, responsive styling, and gameplay in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added Backrooms-inspired rooms, cartoon planes/enemies, waves, upgrades, pause, sound toggle, game-over, and victory screens.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser console showed zero errors after fixing an initialization bug.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. If further verification is needed, test full play through level transitions and mobile touch controls.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, controls, rooms, enemies, upgrades, and UI screens.
- `index.html`: Game page and canvas.
- `style.css`: Responsive game layout and overlays.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; browser testing was performed at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Temporary screenshot files were removed after visual checks.

content.text:
Built **Plane Tame** as a playable browser game in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.

It includes 10 Backrooms-themed rooms, cartoon planes and enemies, auto-fire, upgrades, pickups, dash and pause controls, and a final victory screen. Keyboard and pointer/touch controls are supported. I assumed “lots of levels” meant a 10-room run.

Verified the game script with `node --check` and checked the browser for console errors.
